steps.text: Vehicles have two meters that measure motion. Let's see what each one does.
Start driving and watch both dials as the vehicle moves.
The speedometer shows the speed right now (how fast you're going). The odometer adds up the total distance travelled.
So speedometer = current speed, odometer = total distance. The trip meter is an odometer you can reset for a single journey.

coach.mission: Tell apart what the speedometer and odometer measure.
whenStuck: Drive and watch both dials change.
Ask: which shows speed now, and which adds up distance?
whenWrong: Speedometer = current speed; odometer = total distance travelled.
The odometer keeps counting distance even when speed changes.
whenCorrect: Right — the speedometer shows how fast, the odometer shows how far.
Good — the trip meter is a resettable odometer for one journey.
coach.done: You've learned what the speedometer and odometer measure. Move on when you're ready.
